sources.entry: claude-control by Sverrir Sigurdsson - A native macOS Electron dashboard that auto-discovers running Claude Code CLI sessions and shows live per-session status, git changes, PR checks, and conversation previews across repos and worktrees — and can focus, send input to, approve or reject, kill, or spawn sessions from one place. Electron + Next.js + TypeScript, local-only, via an auto-installed stat

summary.one_liner: A native macOS Electron dashboard that auto-discovers running Claude Code CLI sessions and shows their live status, git changes, PR checks, and conversation previews, with quick actions to focus, approve/reject, or manage them.
keywords: see what my claude agents are doing
manage several coding agents from one window
summary.what_it_does: Finds running claude CLI processes through the process table and maps each to its working directory and transcript file, using Claude Code hook events when available and mtime-based discovery otherwise. It classifies each session as Working, Idle, Waiting, Errored, or Finished, primarily from hook events with a CPU and transcript heuristic fallback. It shows git branch, changed files and line counts, plus open PR status via the gh CLI, including CI rollup, review decision, and merge conflicts. Each session card shows the last assistant message, active tool, and user prompt, and can extract Linear issue context from MCP tool results. From the dashboard you can focus the terminal tab, approve or reject permission prompts, send input, open editor, git GUI, Finder or PR, and create new sessions with worktree support. Data is derived on each request from the process table, hook event files and JSONL transcripts, with no database.
use_cases: monitor several Claude Code sessions across repos at once
approve or reject Claude permission prompts without switching windows
check CI and review status of PRs opened by agent sessions
jump to the terminal tab running a given Claude session
create new Claude sessions in git worktrees
clean up worktrees and branches after agent work
how_to_run: npm run electron:build (produces DMG and ZIP in dist/)
notable: Hook-based status classification from Claude Code lifecycle events, with a heuristic fallback
Tab-level focus and keystroke control for iTerm2, Terminal.app, kitty, WezTerm and cmux
Approve or reject permission prompts from the dashboard, including via tmux send-keys without terminal focus
Installs its hook events into ~/.claude/settings.json automatically on first launch
No database; all state is derived on every request from processes, hook files and transcripts
caveats: macOS only, because terminal integration uses AppleScript
Full tab focus needs extra setup for kitty (remote control config and restart) and iTerm2 hotkey windows (Python API enabled); Ghostty, Warp and Alacritty get only basic app-level focus
Requires Node.js 18 or newer and the GitHub CLI for PR detection; tmux is optional
